{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox Hurling All-Ireland |year=2020 |image = Croke park hogan stand.jpg |image_size = 250 |dates= 24 October - 13 December 2020 |teams=10 |leinster= Kilkenny |munster= Limerick |ulster= |matches= 17 |poty= |team= Limerick |titles= 9th |captain= [[Declan Hannon]] |manager= [[John Kiely (Limerick hurler)|John Kiely]] |team2= Waterford |captain2= [[Conor Prunty]] |manager2= [[Liam Cahill]] |totalgoals= 41 (2.41 per game) |totalpoints= 787 (46.29 per game) |topscorer= [[File:Colours of Waterford.svg|20px|Border]] [[Stephen Bennett (hurler)|Stephen Bennett]] (1–54) |previous=[[2019 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2019]] |next=[[2021 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2021]] }} The '''2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' (SHC) was the 133rd staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier [[inter-county]] [[hurling]] tournament, since its establishment in [[1887 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1887]]. The 2020 fixtures were announced in October 2019.{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/allireland-champions-tipperary-to-begin-munster-campaign-against-waterford-38581123.html|title =All-Ireland champions Tipperary to begin Munster campaign against Waterford|date=10 October 2019|work=Irish Independent|access-date=11 October 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/clare-and-cork-facing-tough-schedule-in-2020-munster-championship-954330.html|title=Clare and Cork facing tough schedule in 2020 Munster Championship|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=2 October 2019|access-date=3 October 2019}} Games were initially scheduled to begin on 9 May 2020. Due to the [[impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on Gaelic games]], the competition was delayed before beginning on 24 October 2020 and ending on 13 December 2020.{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/310051|title=GAA postpone inter-county championships until further notice|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=14 April 2020|access-date=14 April 2020}}{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2020/0626/1149765-2020-hurling-and-football-championships-finalised/|title =Saturday football final as 2020 Championships finalised|date=26 June 2020|work=[[RTÉ Sport]] |access-date=30 June 2020}} [[Laois county hurling team|Laois]] returned to the [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|Leinster Championship]] for the first time since [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|2017]], replacing [[Carlow county hurling team|Carlow]] who were relegated in 2019.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/joe-mcdonagh-cup-laois-westmeath-4703971-Jun2019/|title=Laois produce stunning second half display to capture Joe McDonagh Cup|publisher=The 42|date=30 June 2019|access-date=3 October 2019|first=Brendan|last=Graham}}{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2019/0608/1054201-wexford-line-up-kilkenny-showdown-and-relegate-carlow/|title=Wexford line up Kilkenny showdown and relegate Carlow|work=[[RTÉ Sport]] |date=8 June 2019|access-date=3 October 2019|first=Ronan|last=Fagan}} [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary]] entered the competition as the [[2019 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champion]], attempting to retain the title for the first time since [[1965 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1965]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/tipperary-kilkenny-hurling-4-4771440-Aug2019/|title=Tipperary power to All-Ireland glory to claim 14-point win over Kilkenny|publisher=The 42|date=18 August 2019|access-date=3 October 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} [[Galway county hurling team|Galway]] eliminated Tipperary with a defeat in the All-Ireland SHC quarter-final. In the [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|final]], held at [[Croke Park]] on 13 December 2020, [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] won the competition with a 0–30 to 0–19 win against [[Waterford county hurling team|Waterford]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40189962.html|title=Superb Limerick regain All-Ireland title with emphatic win|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=13 December 2020|access-date=13 December 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}} It was the team's ninth title, as well as a first title since [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2018]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-champions-following-slick-performance-to-see-off-waterford-39858480.html|title=Limerick are All-Ireland champions following slick performance to see off Waterford|date=13 December 2020|work=Irish Independent|accessdate= 11 May 2021}}{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/gaa/hurling/news/30554/12160285/limerick-0-30-waterford-0-19-treaty-triumph-to-regain-all-ireland-title|title=Limerick 0–30 Waterford 0–19: Treaty triumph to regain All-Ireland title|date=13 December 2020|work=Sky Sports|accessdate= 11 May 2021}} Waterford's [[Stephen Bennett (hurler)|Stephen Bennett]] was the competition's top scorer, finishing with 1–54. {{TOC limit|4}} ==Format== {{cleanup MOS |section |date=June 2023 |reason=[[MOS:BOLD]]}} Initially, the 2020 All-Ireland hurling championship format was to feature five-team groups in both Leinster and Munster and the two Joe McDonagh Cup finalists in the format introduced in 2018 for an initial three-year period. At the GAA Congress on 29 February 2019 it was decided to expand the Leinster Hurling Championship from five to six teams, beginning in 2021. This meant there would be no relegation from the Leinster Hurling Championship in 2020 and that the winners of the Joe McDonagh Cup would be promoted.{{cite web |title=Changes to Leinster SHC and Joe McDonagh Cup formats gets the go-ahead |url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Article/Index/309173 |website=www.hoganstand.com |publisher=Hogan Stand |access-date=1 March 2020}} Due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland|COVID-19 pandemic in Ireland]], some changes were announced on 26 June 2020. The format reverted to knockout provincial championships, along with qualifiers, similar to the 2017 format. The two Joe McDonagh Cup finalists did not compete in the senior championship. The draws for the Munster and Leinster Senior Hurling Championships took place live on RTÉ's [[Six One]] news on Friday 26 June.{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2020/0625/1149604-munster-and-leinster-hurling-draws-live-on-rte/|title =Munster and Leinster hurling draws live on RTÉ|date=26 June 2020|work=[[RTÉ Sport]] |access-date=30 June 2020}} {{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/gaa-december-all-ireland-5133792-Jun2020/|title =December All-Ireland final dates confirmed as GAA unveil 2020 championship plan|date=26 June 2020|work=The 42|access-date=30 June 2020}}{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2020/0626/1149901-watch-the-munster-and-leinster-shc-draws-live/|title =Recap: Munster and Leinster hurling draws |date=26 June 2020|work=[[RTÉ Sport]]|access-date=30 June 2020}} === Leinster Championship === '''Participating counties (5):''' [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]], [[Galway GAA|Galway]], [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]], [[Laois GAA|Laois]], [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] '''Quarter-finals (1 match):''' This are one match between the first two teams drawn – the other three teams receive a bye. One team is eliminated at this stage while the winners advance to the semi-finals. '''Semi-finals (2 matches):''' The winners of the quarter-final join the other three teams to make up the semi-final pairings. Two teams are eliminated at this stage while the winners advance to the final. '''Final (1 match)''': The winners of the two semi-finals contest this game. The Leinster champions advance to the All-Ireland semi-finals and the Leinster runners-up advance to the All-Ireland quarter-finals. === Munster Championship === '''Participating counties (5):''' [[Clare GAA|Clare]], [[Cork GAA|Cork]], [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]], [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]], [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] '''Quarter-finals (1 match):''' This are one match between the first two teams drawn – the other three teams receive a bye. One team is eliminated at this stage while the winners advance to the semi-finals. '''Semi-finals (2 matches):''' The winners of the quarter-final join the other three teams to make up the semi-final pairings. Two teams are eliminated at this stage while the winners advance to the final. '''Final (1 match)''': The winners of the two semi-finals contest this game. The Munster champions advance to the All-Ireland semi-finals and the Munster runners-up advance to the All-Ireland quarter-finals. === All-Ireland Championship === '''Qualifiers round 1 (2 matches):''' The six teams who failed to reach a provincial final enter this round. These are two matches between the first four teams drawn – the other two teams receive a bye. Two teams are eliminated at this stage while the winners advance to the qualifiers round 2. '''Qualifiers round 2 (2 matches):''' The winners of the qualifiers round 1 join the other two teams to make up the qualifiers round 2 pairings. Two teams are eliminated at this stage while the winners advance to the quarter-finals. '''Quarter-finals (2 matches):''' The winners of the preliminary quarter-finals join the Leinster and Munster runners-up to make up the quarter-final pairings. Teams who may have already met in the provincial championships are kept apart in separate quarter-finals. Two teams are eliminated at this stage while the winners advance to the semi-finals. '''Semi-finals (2 matches):''' The winners of the quarter-finals join the Leinster and Munster champions to make up the semi-final pairings. Teams who may have met in the provincial finals are kept apart in separate semi-finals where possible. Two teams are eliminated at this stage while the winners advance to the final. '''Final (1 match):''' The two winners of the semi-finals contest this game. == Team changes == === From Championship === Relegated to the [[Christy Ring Cup]] * [[Offaly county hurling team|Offaly]] The single match between Clare and Limerick played on 25 October 2020 was both the [[2020 National Hurling League|National Hurling League Final]] and the Munster Hurling Championship Quarter-final.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-john-kiely-hurling-clare-5245195-Oct2020/|title =A trophy for Limerick in strange times, league leaders after struggle and scoring stars shine|date= 25 October 2020|work=The 42|access-date=27 October 2020}} * Limerick retained the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] for the first time since [[1981 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1981]]. * It was the first Munster final between Limerick and Waterford since 2007. * It was the first ever All-Ireland final between Limerick and Waterford. * It was only the third All-Ireland final that ended goalless, the others being the [[2004 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final]] and the [[1999 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final]]. == Live televised games == [[RTÉ Television|RTÉ]], the national broadcaster in [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] provided the majority of the live television coverage of the hurling championship in the fourth year of a five-year deal running from 2017 until 2021.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2019/0430/1046541-munster-double-bill-to-open-rtes-championship-schedule/ |title =Munster double bill to open RTÉ's Championship schedule|date=30 April 2019|work=[[RTÉ Sport]] |access-date=30 April 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/rte-gaa-coverage-2-5234967-Oct2020/|title =No shortage of live championship action as RTÉ unveil upcoming GAA coverage|date= 16 October 2020|work=The 42|access-date=16 October 2020}}[[Sky Sports]] also broadcast a number of matches and have exclusive rights to some games.
